summary: Thoas (Ancient Greek: Θόας, "fleet, swift") is one of Penelope's suitors in Apollodorus' catalogue — among the fifty-seven wooers from Dulichium who wasted Odysseus' house and were slain with the rest when the king returned. He is attested only in that list and must be kept distinct from the better-known kings Thoas of Aetolia and of Lemnos, and from Penelope's Spartan brother of the same name.

sections.heading: Among the wooers
paragraphs: Apollodorus (Epitome 7.26–7.27) lists Thoas among the fifty-seven suitors from Dulichium, named with Amphinomus, Demoptolemus, Amphimachus, Euryalus, Paralus, and many others who occupied Odysseus' palace. Homer does not give a full name-list of the Dulichians; this Thoas appears only in the later catalogue.
With the other suitors he was shot dead by Odysseus, aided by Eumaeus, Philoetius, and Telemachus.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: The name is crowded: not thoas-aetolia (son of Andraemon, Aetolian captain at Troy), not the Lemnian or Taurian kings, not Penelope's Spartan brother son of Icarius, and not thoas-giant of the Gigantomachy. This node is the Dulichian wooer alone.
